objective: Qualify fail-closed deployment admission, migration fencing, canary promotion, operational rollback, and recovery evidence without granting model output authority.

sources.conclusion: Deployment consumers should verify provenance describing where, when, and how an artifact was produced, including builder identity, inputs, and output subjects.
Controlled rollout, revision history, rollout status, canary behavior, and rollback to a previous revision are explicit deployment safety mechanisms.

implementation.signature_scope: existing local validation key only; not an operator production key or HSM/KMS attestation root

signed_deployment_fixture.signature_scope: existing local validation key only; not a production signing root

existing_m78_deployment_supervisor_qemu.scope: existing bounded QEMU supervisor artifact; not independent multi-host deployment qualification

release_gate_change.requires: signed structured deployment-governance JSON in addition to artifact, advisory, accelerator, and replication evidence

limitations: No external independent deployment controller or operator separation was available in the sandbox.
No live multi-host worker migration or networked service orchestration was exercised.
No production HSM, KMS, Vault, or hardware-rooted deployment approval was exercised.
The M78 QEMU regression uses the existing recovered build profile and is recorded as bounded historical supervisor validation, not current production deployment proof.
Irreversible external side effects and compensation workflows require an operational environment and remain unqualified.
The overall production release gate remains blocked by operator key ceremony, independent builder, physical accelerator, CVE operations, external security review, and deployment governance inputs.
claims_not_made: No claim of production deployment readiness.
No claim of live cluster migration safety.
No claim of real-world rollback of irreversible external actions.
No claim that model output can authorize deployment.
